label: Elenctic defense of a first principle: In Metaphysics IV.4,1006a11–28, Aristotle distinguishes…
term: elenctic defense of a first principle
definition: In Metaphysics IV.4,1006a11–28, Aristotle distinguishes demonstration from an elenctic showing whose starting concession is that the interlocutor signify something to himself and another. Determinate signification is extracted from that concession; the opponent who submits is responsible for the premise. This records the proposed dialectical method, not an automatically successful proof of every proposition indispensable to an inquiry, and not a universal epistemic-to-ontic bridge.
note: Formal boundary: FIRST_PRINCIPLE_ENTITLEMENT_AND_PRESUPPOSITION_1 remains prose-only. Its consumer is statement 73a6cf93-1a16-51a5-a208-deb90b3284e9, with no Lean declaration or consuming argument at the audited baseline. An occurring utterance alone is not determinate signification. OPEN: represent what an interlocutor signifies, the same meaning across assertion and denial, and the concession-to-PNC inference without assuming the conclusion. A meaningful concession is the intended example; mere token occurrence is excluded. This is an encoding obligation, not an objection to the recorded reading.
